page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the custom ARM-based Alibaba YiTian710 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 2.75 GHz without hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on a KVM hypervisor. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard workloads. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests fall within the middle 50% tier, as do the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. Memory read bandwidth is strong for small cached blocks at 407.26 GB/sec, though large block uncached write bandwidth drops to a weaker 25.44 GB/sec. The instance shows poor performance in cryptographic operations, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 10%. LLM inference for medium 7B models is also limited, yielding 4.54 tokens/sec.

Utilizing the ARM64 architecture, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads that do not require specialized x86 instructions or heavy cryptographic processing. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.51 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a PassMark database score of 4162.86 and 6.71 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Other suitable workloads include software compilation and general text processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose instance powered by a 2.75 GHz Alibaba YiTian710 processor with 4 dedicated physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier for general compute, software compilation, and text processing, though it exhibits weaker results in large-block memory writes, image processing, and ray tracing. Cryptographic performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark encryption test scoring in the bottom 10%. Qualitatively, the ARM-based architecture provides resource-dense efficiency for workloads such as static web serving, Redis caching, and standard database operations that do not rely on x86-specific instruction sets.
